RUSH Match History

SyN and Biohazard .VS. Stauz Quo and Dante Jackson from Playaz Inc.

Result: Win and then attacked by Biohazard and dragged into the van, being drived away.

NO MATCH 

 Signature Moves 

Confession:  An Inverted DDT

 Mastermind Death Flip:  A double moonsault (usually off of a laddder)

 Germancanrana:  A hurricanrana pin

 Hit it up:  A solid Superkick flip

 Business:  A Senton Bomb

 Germanality:  I 540 splash pin

SyN was born and raised in Germany as Steff Neirlinger, an average kid. He had a brother and a mom. His dad a was special enforcer for the army and was shot on the night that SyN was born.

SyN and his brother, Sven went on with normal lifes in an average house with friends and everything.

Then one after noon, when SyN was just 12, his mom had gotten tickets on a boat that was travelling to New York city. It was an offer for a new life and to be more than just average. There was just one thing wrong.

SyN's mom had only gotten two tickets. It was all she could get and afford at the time. SyN was 12 and Sven, 14.

SyN's mom figured that Sven was old enough and took SyN, who wasn't old enough to live on his own, with her to America, leaving Sven behind.

New York had been great. SyN's mom had got a good job at a bakery on the street down from SyN's apartment.

SyN went to school, made friends and explored new things.

At the age of sixteen, SyN's mom asked SyN what he wanted to do with his life. Facinated with wrestling and the high-flyers at the time, SyN decided to start training for wrestling, hoping a break in a federation would come along.

SyN went under the guidance of Dabadindoo Shackabargeay, a wrestling analogy expert that lived down the street to SyN.

There, SyN learned Karate and Martial Arts, but more importantly, how to fly like an eagle.

You see, SyN was at his full size of 6'0, 240 at the time, which was a bit larger than the high flyers in the wrestling business but with help from Dabadindoo, who always believed in him, SyN learnt how to do it like the pros, doing flips and moonsaults and anything crazy.

SyN now had all the wrestling talent, and all he needed was a federation.

An ad was showing around the city of the New True Internet Championship Wrestling and how it would be opening soon under the guidance of White Mexican. SyN applied, a hopeful like some of the others and miraculously got accepted.

SyN started in the fed a nobody, feuding with another nobody, Karep. After battling with Karep for a week, a match came up. And Extreme title match in a Playboy mansion match.

SyN had won, using all his strength. He had became the NTICW Extreme Championship.

From that point on, SyN was no longer a nobody but someone who had impressed everybody in the locker room, even joining forces with Scott Taylor, Andi the Magnificent, and Teresa Tomas to form the Ultimate Opposition.

SyN was riding the high life.

Then an e-mail came. And e-mail that would put SyN through a whole lot more.

The email was from a man named Nick Ramsey, a terrorist group that threatened to put New York on fire and burn it down by placing six bombs in three buildings in New York.

After going through a lot and making some new friends, SyN finally made it to Nick Ramsey, only to find out that the man wasn't Nick Ramsey, but Sven Neirlinger, his brother!

After a grueling battle, SyN pushed the about button at the last second to save New York.

Nick Ramsey however, escaped in a plane to who knows wherem disappearing.

Saving the world in time, SyN went back to America, only to find out that NTICW had closed, Scott Taylor was in a different fed, and SyN was now a member of RUSH wrestling.

What will happen in RUSH for SyN? The story can be written in any direction...

tenures.bio:
Clem came from a small town, called Lemmon, South Dakota.  He 

always dreamed of being a wrestler, though, he was always deemed too small, 

so he got a job close to the action.  He joined the wrestling world as ring 

crew.

He happily worked along side the wrestlers, constantly the butt of jokes, due to his looks, and redneck ways, but he still felt like he was living his dream.  He joined CCW, as ring crew, and stayed there for quite a 

while.

At least, until his dream came true.  An injured Cianan, CCW champion at 

the time, and owner of CCW, as well.  Became injured, and his increasing 

paranoia caused him to look for some 'muscle.' no one applied, exscept 

Clem.  Cianan begrudgingly took him on, and gave Clem a shot at being a 

>wrestler, which Clem has never forgotten and to this day thanks, and is loyal towards his 'dream maker' Cianan.

As The Masked Mullet, he struggled to over come adversity, beating opponents like Bojangles The Klown, and Devyl, and eventually winning #1 contendership to a hardcore title.  The title shot never came.  However, he did make quite a name for himself being as a 'hardcore icon.' (though, he never won the title)

After struggling and adversity, he managed to beat several people, and win 

the newly re-instated Light Weight Champion, over the likes of Kyle 

'Velocity' Lamen, Kensuke Suzahara, and Jesse Ramey.

After a small, and rather painful experiance in the MET Tournament, (and 

losing to Lilith in a house show).  He sank back into obscurity

Commonly Used Moves:

Hurricanrana, Body Splash, Cross Body, Knife Edge Chops, Top Rope Leg Drop, Bear Hug, Scoop Slam, Off the Top Clothesline, Bulldog, Missle Drop Kick, Drop Toe Hold, Spinning Toe Hold, Spring Board 3rd Rope Splash Suicida.

tenures.bio:
The sun had set, leaving a warm glow all across Kingston, as a baby boy was born. The hot, sticky air of that late August evening left the mother absolutely exhausted. She was in no mood for the screaming baby beside her, his round belly glistening in the dying sun and the tears trickling down from his eyes. The only comfort he could find was from a congratulatory basket of fruit on the bedside table.

The early years of his life were spent crying for his parents, they were in no situation to look after the baby and had to work much more to try and supply for his greedy appetites. They had struggled to settle on a name for him, dozens of different ideas and suggestions had come and gone. Joseph was what they eventually called him, an old granddad had been named this and it seemed to suit the growing child.

The very first day that young Joseph went out on his own, to play with the children outside, he ran back in as quickly as his stubby legs would carry him. He couldn’t stand the endless teasing and mocking. For lack of his mother most of the time, Joseph still sucked his thumb and had a generally less than independent character. With his parents gone more often than not, and no children befriending him at all, Joseph would find comfort in anything else he could find. He carried a pale blue blanket around with him, but it was torn and scratched by a cat from a nearby neighbour’s house.

After continuously searching, and finding flaws in each or having it taken from him somehow, Joseph had one last attempt… fruit. It all started with a juicy mango, which had been intended for eating after his meal. Joseph cuddled it and talked to it, never being mocked by it. He continued his friendship with all the fruit he could find, greeting each one and talking at length with them about his problems and feelings. This lead to great trouble at school, his first day he had witnessed a banana being squashed and thrown against a wall. He strode up to the older boy and raised his fists.

“Don’ beh foo, yah rahtid fruit killer!” Joseph screeched to the bewildered boy.

Joseph was dead-set and punched the boy’s face with all his might, knocking him to the ground with a bloody nose. Incidents such as this continued, forcing Joseph into seemingly endless amounts of time in detention. He was a troublemaker, who never meant any harm. The children now had something greater to mock him with, his odd obsession with fruit. He was totally ignorant and unaware, he thought he was the only one in the right and everybody was insane. These fruit became more and more his best friends, and his only friends.

As he paid more and more attention to his fruit chums, he knew less and less. Information would not stick in his brain; he barely had the basic knowledge needed. His parents were becoming more and more worried about Joseph’s problem. Child psychiatrists, doctors and many old wives’ home remedies made absolutely no impact. The best suggestion was to get Joseph involved in some sort of activity that would eventually deter his attention and bring him in to the real world. And so Joseph was forcefully enrolled into a small wrestling school that had recently opened over half an hours journey outside of Kingston. Joseph would make the journey every week, learn different holds and takedowns then make the journey back home. He was good at it, no doubt about that, but he wasn’t focused and didn’t put all of his energy into it as had been hoped by his parents.

During the later half of his teenage years, Joseph did get into wrestling more and enjoyed doing it. He was one of the best in his class, but seen as the bottom for his problem with fruit. He was treated as if disabled, not all there in his mind. But nobody could hold him back, as he pushed harder and harder on himself. It lead to a transfer to an American school, and even less acceptance. Nobody understood why he talked to fruit, and why he thought they talked back to him. Considered a joke and pain point of mockery, Joseph Banner was nicknamed Joe Bananas. Giggles could be heard whenever he asked advice from a grape, or if he talked about his day with a raspberry. Joe Bananas was a joke to everyone, and has been ever since then. But his erratic and unpredictable style in the ring has lead him far, and has kept his loyal friendship with fruit stronger than ever.

tenures.bio:
Robert Amanze was a young teenager who at the age of 17 had 

everything. Fast car,beautiful girlfriend, straight A student and soccer

supertstar. He was doing very well at college but knew he wasn’t happy as his 

real love was soccer. He was on the books of London’s finest soccer team Arsenal, and 

felt that his future career lied here. So at the age of 18 decided to give 

up his studies and concentrate on soccer. He didn’t get the blessing of his 

parents but promised to prove them wrong and become a professional 

soccer player. Robert was already in the Arsenal youth team and managed within 

a year to get into the reserve team. He was then told on the eve of his 19th 

birthday that he was to be on the bench for the home game against London 

rivals Spurs. Robert was overjoyed but knew he was only in the squad due to 

a recent pile up of injuries. Robert however knew if he got the chance to 

come on would surely impress. 

Sadly however the morning of the game during a light training session Robert 

injured his left knee badly. He was trying very hard, some say too hard and 

fell awkwardly on his knee after a slide tackle. Robert immediately knew 

something was wrong and was told by the surgeon who operated on his knee 

that he would never play top level soccer again. 

Robert was devastated and felt that his life was over at the young age of 

19. He decided with the advice of his parents to go back to school and do a 

course in marketing as he had a real knack for this in his youth. Sadly 

though he quit after just 6 months. It was quite clear he had not recovered 

from the disappointment at seeing his soccer career finish and decided to 

take some time out. 

One evening after a massive row with his parents Robert left home and 

decided to look for a flat. He moved up north and decided to get a part 

time job in his local pub. It was here one day while during his rounds he 

met up with his old school friend Mike Taylor. Mike was part of the same 

sports scene Robert was once part of at school and they talked intensely. 

Mike from what Robert could remember was once a very talented Greco-Roman 

wrestler. However as they carried on speaking Robert was informed Mike's 

promising career had been cut short by an recurring back injury. It was then 

that Mike informed Robert that he was now a scout for little known British 

wrestling federation The WFA (wrestling for anybody). It became quite 

obvious to Robert that Mike was looking for new talent as the British 

wrestling scene hadn’t really taken off yet. Mike spoke at how he could 

recall that Robert was once a very good athlete and asked if he was 

interested. Robert politely declined and said he had only seen wrestling 

briefly on t.v and was convinced the whole thing was just fake. Mike 

reassured Robert it wasn’t and that just some of the big matches in the us 

were fixed. Mike gave Robert his number and Robert politely excepted even 

though knowing he would probably never use it. 

One rainy day Robert was driving home from work when his car skidded into a 

nearby electric cable. He escaped unhurt but was told by doctors he was 

very lucky the cable hadn’t had been too high an voltage. Robert then knew 

his life wasn’t set out for nine to five jobs and decided to try and make 

something of his life. It was a week later when something of a ray of light 

came Robert's way. He was reading the newspaper when an advert for the WFA 

was plastered on the middle page. The WFA were coming down to London in 

three months and were suddenly in much demand. Wrestlers such as Chris Luck 

and the Unknown had brought back respect to British wrestling. Livewire 

couldn’t turn down this opportunity and decided to ring Mike who gladly 

offered Robert a trial and try and help him compete for the forthcoming 

London tour. Robert trained with Mike intensely during those three months 

and it came quite apparent that Robert was still an excellent athlete and 

was picking up the basic wrestling moves very easily. Robert was then given 

a trial a week before the tour and didn’t disappoint. He won the match 

against one of the feds useless jobbers by using a modified sleeper hold 

taught to him by Mike. After the match a tired, hurt and sweating Robert was 

told by the WFA president that he was in. Robert was overjoyed and instantly 

accepted the invitation to join the fed on their tour. Robert slowly moved up 

the ranks under his name as Robert Amanze but it became quite apparent WFA 

were still a small time fed and they were forced to let Robert go due to 

their small budget. Robert joined numerous small feds such as the PCW2, XWA and the NTICW to keep up his fitness 

and it was during one XWA house show that he was spotted by the RUSH president Jeremy Howard. Robert was told by him that he liked what he saw but felt for Robert to 

survive in RUSH he would have to get a new persona and gimmick as his 

current one just wasn’t good enough. Robert then thought of a time when he 

was given direction (after the car accident) and a name his sports teacher 

once gave him for his tenacity 'Livewire'. Jeremy Howard loved it and a 

formal contract was written and the rest as they say is history.

signature_moves: The Nile High -Spring board star dust press [With his opponents down on the canvas, Pharaoh runs towards the ropes and using his amazing balance leaps onto the top cable, without a moment too soon he leaps back off and using the elastic in the ropes propels himself through the air in the form of a Star dust press before landing perfectly onto his unsuspecting opponent.] Wrath of Horus -Insane Dive from a high point in the arena [Pharaoh, obviously feeling suicidal, drags his opponent somewhere in the arena that he feels is a suitable place to position them in preparation for this crazy move. After he’s found his place he looks for a place to climb and before long he finds a height he feels fit to jump from and so without further delay Pharaoh dives from the high point landing his opponent with a suicidal splash.] Treasure of a Pharaoh -Twisting, spinning, springboard plancha [Pharaoh, like the Nile High, runs at the ropes and spring boards off, this time his opponent is standing but they are completely knocked off their feet as Pharaoh spins and Twists his way through the air towards them and finally lands them with a plancha.] Lotus Spring -Spear driving opponent out of the ring [Pharaoh lunges forward at his opponent and, driving his shoulder into their ribs, continues to compel them backwards in a spear-like fashion until finally both the Pharaoh and his opponent fall from the ring through the ropes landing on the harsh ground below.] Valley of the Kings -Death Valley driver spun into a reverse falling DDT [Pharaoh picks his opponent up in a basic fireman’s carry position and then using his strength and balance spins his unlucky opponent into a falling reverse DDT landing them on the back of their head with great force.] Ancient Belief -Hanging Tiger bomb [Pharaoh sets his foe up in the position of a Powerbomb, he brings them up so as it would seem that he were performing an ordinary Powerbomb but as he brings them back down to the mat he stalls so that the victim is hanging in mid arm only by his arms strength. Then when it would seem he isn’t going to drop them in a Powerbomb he drives them down violently onto the back of their neck folding them up like an accordion.] The Unravellment -Tilt-a-whirl reverse DDT [Pharaoh whips his opponents into the ropes and as they are coming back towards him he scoops them up quickly onto his shoulder in the form of a tilt a whirl. Abruptly he salutes the crowd and then flips them over his shoulder catching them into mid air with a reverse DDT.] Catacomb horror -Overhead, spinning belly to back Suplex [Pharaoh locks his opponent up in position for a belly to back throw but before he tosses them overhead he spins them around twice and then abruptly throws them over head.] Cairo Conundrum -450 degree knee drop [Pharaoh ascends the top turn buckle, his opponent out cold on the ground below, he salutes the crowd arrogantly and then without consequence he takes to the air, performing a 450 degree dive before landing knee first in his victims ribs.]
tenures.bio:
What is important about him has already been said. Some heard the whispers, and some didn’t…some…were simply told. It is known that he was born in Cairo, Egypt and remained there for years until he had gained total awareness of the world about him. He studied for a scholarship in ancient history and went on to study archaeology. The man they call The Pharaoh is the only one who knows the truth, whatever that may be, and he doesn’t feel like telling it now – maybe he never will. He isn’t your average man. He is something you’ve never seen before. He’s out to prove a point to his Gods – he is his own new hope.  



He is Titu Xansiv...The Pharaoh

tenures.style: Power with some technical wrestling, and surprising speed for a man his size. He will happily take a clean win, but he rarely has to: a low blow, a foot on the ropes, a referee pulled into harm's way or a blackjack from his pocket usually gets there first.
tenures.bio:
Nobody who meets Cassius Deamont ever has to ask how good he is, because he tells them inside thirty seconds. The silver-haired Torontonian left Canada the first chance he got ("Why do you think I moved away from the place?"), picked up what he insists was a first-rate education, and came out the other side convinced that talent is the only thing that matters and that he has all of it. He goes nowhere without Kathryn, his girlfriend of ten years, and Erica, the two bisexual valets who laugh at his jokes and kick whoever he points at.

Cassius walked into RUSH as the number one contender and opened the very first Adrenaline in Chicago by calling the whole locker room worthless and Jonathan Drachen a pizza delivery boy. By the end of the segment Drachen was flat from a Fall Before Me and Cassius was shaking hands with Chris Matthews. Add Steve Brent and part-owner Tim Walden and you had the Solution, who spent May handcuffing Drachen, Skye Stone, Hiro Saotome and Tex Kelley inside a steel cage and setting the ring on fire, blowing up another ring two weeks later, and putting owner Jeremy Howard to sleep with Cassius's trusty blackjack. The one thing Cassius could not solve was Maxx Crimson, who pinned him in Cleveland.

The cracks started with the valets. Cassius asked Matthews to teach Kathryn and Erica self-defence, Matthews tried a chat-up line on them instead, and Howard played the tape to the whole arena. Somehow it held together at Ignition. Matthews lay down to send Cassius to the main event, Cassius smashed the knees of Drachen's manager Kahlil Anil in a corridor, and one blackjack shot from Walden later he was the first ever RUSH World Champion. He celebrated by blackjacking Drachen, Howard, Matthews and Brent.

As champion he threw in with Boda and the I.R.S. Plan and hired Erica two bodyguards, Rich Cannon and Vulcan Flare. Matthews answered by kidnapping Kathryn and blowing up Cassius's limo. Cassius kept winning anyway, over Tex Kelley, over Matthews in Hartford and over El Spiffy!, usually with Boda standing somewhere nearby. At Crossroads in Washington, Boda proudly named him the new 25 percent owner of RUSH. Cassius had already sold the share to Rush Mason, which left Boda owning nothing at all. Kathryn came home that night, but Boda came to the first blood match with a towel and the blackjack, and Matthews walked out as champion. Boda then put Cassius through the announce table for good measure.

The last anyone saw of him, the first RUSH World Champion was holed up above a Los Angeles nightclub with Kathryn, Erica and a pile of old PCW magazines, reading up on Boda and very nearly admitting that he might have picked his friends badly.
tenures.finisher: Fall Before Me — Cassius puts his opponent's head between his thighs as if for a Pedigree, hooks the arms, then uses his strength to haul them straight up into a reverse tombstone position before swinging them forward and slamming them face first into the mat.

tenures.bio: Matt Elia was the older of two children born to Alexander and Robin Elia. Both Alex and Robin’s family’s were immigrants from Italy. Alexander’s farther was a very rich diplomat and fled Italy once Mussolini began to take control of the country. Fleeing with his money Alexander SR. set up a very well to do business. After Alexander SR. death Alexander Elia Jr. took over the company as well as the inheritance of the billons of dollars that his father had earned. Now cut to a picture perfect meeting of Alex Jr. and Robin the daughter of the other local Boston construction company. As the two tied the knot so did the two companies and the Elia name became a household name…literally as thousands of apartments and homes began to pop up all over Boston with the Elia name imprinted in everyone. Now speed ahead 3 years to a hot and steamy September night in 1976. Sure enough after a long night of you know what Robin Elia walked out of the bathroom with that little pink line. Baby time….Matthew Ryan Elia was born on May 13, 1977. 3 years later on May 6 1980 Chris Elia was born. Cut ahead 13 years. Matt and Chris have been home schooled paid in full by their parents. Both children have received the intellect that most children would be jealous of. The only problem is that both children lack strong friends. Cut ahead 10 more years. Matt has just finished graduate school at Oxford University in England. Although Matt was smart and would most likely have been valedictorian of his high school class, (had he attended) his parent’s money attracted the looks of Oxford. Now surrounded by the smartest and brightest students in the entire world Matt began to become intimidated and would come close to flunking out. In fact the Elia fortune helped him stay in school as long as he did.  Chris on the other hand was beginning school locally in Boston at the University of Harvard. He would eventually go on to graduate Suma Kum Luad of his class. Cut ahead 6 months. Matt and Chris have both decided to take their interest of pro wrestling to work. With the money that they have they both bought wrestling trainers and soon began to train. After lots of hard work…well hard work for the brothers…they found themselves wrestling in Indy gigs. Eventually they landed themselves in a developmental fed known as NZW which would eventually lead them into PCW. After a short stint in PCW the brothers were asked to move to PCW2. After decline the offer they moved to NTICW in which they found much success by capturing the tag tittles. After 2 more times of holding these titles the brothers would eventually go on to be one of the more successful teams of NTICW. After leaving NTICW for PCW again the brothers were again unable to find success and found themselves off the roster both nursing neck injuries. It seemed then that the brothers had disappeared from wrestling all together. But Matt reemerged in the PCW atmosphere. Matt began to produce an extremely popular column known as 20 Questions for Boobie Boy. The column became a cult classic and was read and enjoyed by many. Now after 6 months away from the ring Matt has decided to return. With brother Chris by his side for help Matt hopes to find renewed success in RUSH WRESTLING.

tenures.bio:
Matthias Hunt was born into a German working class family on April 7th 1971. His father, Karl, is an executive within his father’s (Matthias’ grandfather’s) contracting company (the biggest in Northern Germany, third largest in Germany) and his Mother, Kristina, works as a head nurse at the local hospital.

He also has an older brother called Andreas who is five years his senior, who continues the family tradition of working in the family business alongside his father and grandfather. Sister Gina is two years younger and works as a freelance photographer for the numerous local newspapers.

Matthias - or Matt for short - is married to Manchester-born Stephanie and has two children; Carl (4) and Jessica (7). The three of them currently reside in a New York suburb after deciding to move to the United States, as Matt’s wrestling career made the leap across the pond from Europe.

At grammar school at Lons-Sherber Gymnasium (German grammar school) in Hamburg, Matt excelled in his favourite subject; English. He was the polite and well-mannered student, but often had his moments where he would act the class clown to get attention.

He was also the sportsman, although he only had eyes for one sport in particular and it wasn’t wrestling…hell, wrestling wasn’t even known of in Germany until the late 1980’s! Matt’s main love in life was football, or soccer, and often used his size advantage (he was 16st at aged 17) on the pitch. Of course, people debated whether he should chase his dream of following in his hero’s – German football captain Franz Beckenbauer – footsteps and become a professional footballer.

By the time he left the grammar school, Matt was a hefty 17st and stood at 6’4” and had his heart set on playing professional football. However, the top German clubs in the area turned him down because of his abnormal bulk and his dreams of playing the field were slowly fading quickly.

He decided to hop across the English Channel and try a number of English clubs to trial at. Using his vast knowledge of the game, he noticed that the English style was much more physical than his local German approach. So, with this in mind he thought he would be at an advantage and knocked on the doors of certain teams in London area.

But his dream were dashed once more, but it wasn’t the language barrier as Matt had excelled in the English subject at school and spoke the dialect fluently. He was simply too big to be a footballer, despite his young age and talented potential, and to save time and money on other clubs of the country, officials advised that he should change the direction he wanted to go in.

At 20, Matt was obviously crushed and seeked a new career path. But what would he do? He didn’t want to return to Germany, he had tasted the English environment and wanted more, but what exactly?

He obtained a working pass and worked in a supermarket. He wasn’t paid that much a week, but what he did earn was enough to survive. He also found accommodation nearby in a bed and breakfast establishment…again, not ideal living situations, but at least he had a roof over his head and some hot food.

After a few months of stacking shelfs and huffing and puffing in the back stores, he noticed an advertisement for a new wrestling school that was soon opening in the area. He hadn’t given the idea much thought as he’d always had football as his career path. But this appealed to him and after hearing the news that he was “too big for football”, was he too big to be a wrestler?

He enquired and enrolled in the school for a costly fee that took away nearly half of his weekly wage, but Matt didn’t mind and made the necessary sacrifices. He slowly but surely worked on his physic and in-ring style, while suffering taunts about his nationality and often suffering racist remarks.

Instead of reacting face-to-face, Matt took the abuse and worked his frustration off in the ring and gym…it soon paid off and after six or so months in the school, he was up for independent booking by the local small organisations.

However, the small-time promoters often ignored his wrestling ability and prodded at his nationality, for the entertainment factor. Matt began to tour on the indy scene, receiving abuse inside the ring and outside…but this only pushed his determination even further.

As the years rolled by, Matt began excel while trying his best to ignore the taunts and provocation from those working alongside him. He rose up the ladder in the English wrestling scene and got recognition for his technical wrestling ability…as well as his nationality.

It was during a tour of the Greater Manchester area, where Matt met his wife, Stephanie in January 1993. After a whirlwind romance, they married in Salford, Manchester on August 31st 1993 – Stephanie’s birthday. Two years later, in November 1995, baby girl Jessica was born and Carl soon followed in April 1998. While Matt was making changes to his personal life with the marriage and births of two children, his goal of becoming one of the best in the business did not stop for one second.

With the family settled in Manchester and Matt being a big name in the English wrestling scene, he felt it was time for a change and pondered about the hop across the large pond to the North Americas. The family stood by his decision and his mind was made up, the Hunt’s were coming to America!

Matt Hunt is a name well known around the England wrestling scene, especially in the North-West and London. Now that he’s made a big sacrifice and joined the thousands upon thousands of up and coming wrestlers in the United States, how long will it take for Matt Hunt to be a well-known name in these parts?

Only time…and his focus, determination and drive…will tell.

tenures.bio:
Tyler was born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin on February 14th (Valentine’s Day), 1979. At the age of three, his mother, Dana, died during a tragic bicycling accident, leaving Tyler and his father, Aaron, to fend for themselves. This sparked something in Tyler that changed his life forever. He became far more removed from the outside world and was very introspective in his thoughts and words. At one point, he even considered taking his own life. However, while going through rehabilitation after a horrendous knee injury in April 2000, he found the will to continue on living, and became generally happy once again, renewing ties with his family, gaining many new friends, and honing his wrestling skills tremendously. After recently feeling himself about to go into a bout with depression, he decided to get hypnotized to remove any bad memories he had. However, the “hypnotists” – two midget con artists named Tweedledee and Tweedledum – played a practical joke on him, making him believe he was a living, breathing, talking peanut butter and jelly sandwich.

Backstage at the final NTICW Mayhem, a stray puddle of slippery soap would prove to be the most important moment of Valentine's recent life.  Upon falling unconscious, an angel - or so we believe - visited him in his sleeping and offered him the chance to break the hypnosis and find out who he really is.

He accepted.

And now, Valentine must go through the struggle of entertaining millions of people while battling to find his true identity.

Then came Crossroads, RUSH Wrestling's second Pay Per View, in which Valentine finally realized that it's not his past that matters to him, or anyone else for that matter, but the present.

Career History

Tyler's first real wrestling endeavour was in NTICW.  He came out as a rising star in the new Cruiserweight division, which was considered one of the best things to happen to NTICW at the time, becoming the first-ever NTICW Cruiserweight Champion on May 19 at Battle in Brazil.  He would hold the belt for all but the final week before NTICW merged with RUSH.

Tyler Valentine officially became a member of the RUSH roster on June 18, 2002 when NTICW owner Chris Sloboda sold his, along with eighteen other wrestlers', contract over to Jeremy Howard.

Tyler debuted on RUSH Television on July 11, 2002, teaming with Chris Matthews and Tex Kelley in a main-event six-man tag team match against Cassius Deamont, Brock Newbluud, and Boda.  The match was going poorly for the 'good guys' until former NTICW wrestler D-Kay Calyx entered the fray.  Calyx teased a save only to take out Kelley with the Chi-Town DDT.  Newbludd took out Matthews with The Last Call and Boda delivered the Bounced Czech to Valentine, sealing a victory for Deamont, Newbludd, and Boda.  After the match, Calyx further attacked Valentine with the Calyx-O Drop as Adrenaline 9 went off the air, setting up a rivalry that is still going on, fueled by the revelation that Calyx holds a manila folder that supposedly contains secrets of Valentine's past.  On Adrenaline 11, Valentine tried to capture this folder but D-Kay's locker room, but was unsuccessful, being chased out his locker room with a baseball bat.  On Adrenaline 12, Valentine challenged D-Kay to a ladder match - at the top of the ladder is the fabled manila folder.

Come Crossroads, Valentine finally got his hands on the manila folder, only to rip up it into tiny little pieces in front of thousands of confused fans.  His reason?  Who cares, he says.  All Tyler knows is that the only thing that matters now is the present, and anything from his past is simply inconsequential.

After Crossroads, Tyler Valentine noticed something very strange in his best friend, Chris Matthews - he was becomming greedier and more distant by the day.  This all led up to each other foiling each other's title matches with Brock Newbludd, and the falling out of their doomed friendship.  The fact that Brock did nothing to help Valentine from these attacks didn't sit too well with him either.  This rivarly is to be settled once and for all at Rising From the Ashes, on October 13th.

tenures.bio:
The story of Gene Otto Droidman doesn’t even begin with him.  His story begins with a doctor Herbert Jenkins, MD.  HJ has three Phds.  One in medics, one in genes, and one in physics.  Dr. Jenkins is certainly a smart man, if not a genius.

Once out of school entirely his well acquired studies granted him a job within the government.  His work was mainly on medical techniques for soldiers.  Many different projects to help M*A*S*Hs with treating patients quicker, easier, and without flaw.  Little was improved in this area and the projects were abandoned save a few minor authorities.

Dr. Jenkins was moved to more military work, however it is extremely confidential.

Again however, after maybe two or three years basing himself in the government he left and was hired by a drug company.  There he headed up a department on testing drugs on animals and other creatures.  During his research there he noticed that deformities were not rare.  That animals took them with ease.  This made the doctor ponder something about birthing animals and even people.  A possibility of cloning came to mind and Dr. Jenkins started a basement project to clone a rat.  Within just a few months he did in fact clone a rat.  This made him extremely pleased, however, he did not want to tell anyone for he wanted all the credit for his scientific breakthrough.

Keeping it in hiding and doing his own research among his job research, he did little to expand the cloning, but wanted to focus on more of a gene splicing technique.  Once he had heard of the famous Dolly he simply shrugged it off, saying that splicing would be the way to fame.  However, to create such a task, he did in fact find out that even with his amazing financial supply, he did not have enough money to perfect his experiments and research.  So, he looked toward the government for a backing.  This time however, not in the U.S. government, but a western European government that is disclosed at this time.

They did in fact decide that this was extremely useful and worthwhile.  Dr. Jenkin’s backing and assistants were also supreme.  Jenkins decided that his spliced creation would be made up of both bron and brain powers combined into one.  It took six years, two months, and seven days, but in the end, it was possibly the greatest thing ever thought of.  The project called, Genetic Oriented Drone, was named Greg Otto Droidman, or G.O.D. for short.

G.O.D. has been learning, extremely fast as planned, over the past month.  His speech is already perfected, and he reads at a level that surpasses many college graduates.  He is being taught, less educational things, but more life skills.  Mainly however, fighting skills.  Once created, they decided that taking over the intellectual world was done with himself, but to take over the athletic world would be slightly more of a challenge.  That is where Old School Wrestling comes in.  G.O.D. has reviewed many different athletic competitions and organizations and has chosen wrestling, and more importantly, Wrestling Tattler to compete in, against the best of the best.  So the WT will feel the wrath of G.O.D.

Since entering the WT G.O.D. has been in two different organizations.  Those being New True Internet Championship Wrestling and RUSH Wrestling.

In NTICW G.O.D. had minor success as the Extreme Champion.  This championship he won from one Markus Sinniatti.  He would later lose that title to William 'Biohazard' Perry.  That federation soon closed after G.O.D.'s title loss though and much of that roster was moved to the promotion RUSH.

G.O.D. has been in RUSH since July 11 and has taken many people's attention.  Unlike in NTICW G.O.D. is cheered rather than hated by many people.  He is a monster of a man and the biggest, most powerful 'man' in RUSH.  His success is that he won the RUSH Network Championship at the Pay-Per-View Crossroads from Scott Cage.  The future certianly holds greater things for this up-and-comer and only time will tell what they are.  Needless to say though God giveth, but G.O.D. taketh away... soon all of RUSH will find that out.

G.O.D.'s Favorite Things

1. Strawberries

2. Amusement Parks

3. Wrestling

4. Pillows

5. Sugar

Dr. Jenkins' Favorite Things

1. G.O.D.

2. Medicine

3. Teaching

4. Cotton Lab Coats

5. Chocolate Milk

tenures.bio:
Not much was known about the man they call “The Innovator” before he entered the Millenium Wrestling Federation in early September of 2000. He was a drifter who bounced around on the Japan and Mexico scene, never staying in one place for a extended period of time. In Mexico, he earned the nickname “The Innovator” by putting on great matches night after night for only the minimal of wage. The name was set in stone when he first preformed his self-taught finisher, The Skytwister Press in his final match before entering the MWF. He looked at the MWF as a chance to make some money in the sport he loves and quickly jumped on board with the federation.

Brock’s first match in an American ring was against now PCW world champion Frisco. Though he put out a 110% effort he fell short in then end and lost. Then, MWF introduced the newly crafted Rising Star title, and Brock and Frisco would do battle for out. This time, Brock came out on top making his the first ever MWF Rising Star champion. He would later go on to become the MWF Rising Star champ one more time. A few weeks after Brock moved up to the main circuit of the MWF he scored a win over TV champ Thalokos, making him the new TV champ. The TV win, also caused the one of the biggest feuds in MWF/PCW history, one with the late Judas Steele. Steele wanted the title, and would get it by any means necessary. Then, Steele raised the level of the feud, by kidnapping Brock’s girlfriend and MWF reporter, Tiffany Jacobs.

Brock debuted in PCW at its first PPV, Dawning. He debuted by punking out PCW’s newly crowned TV champ Revenant and challenging him to a match for his title. Brock never got the chance to face the cave dweller , for he was sent to jail the night of their match. His replacement…Brock’s arch nemesis, Judas Steele, who still had Tiffany. Judas beat Brock after interference by his bodyguard Bruno.

A match was set between to end the war. A triple cage, Hell in a Cell match, with Tiffany locked in a cage on top of the other two. The stakes were high for the match, if Brock won, he got Tiffany’s freedom, if he lost, he would never wrestle in a PCW ring again. The match was a bloodbath filled with high spots and dangerous maneuvers. It could be one of the most emotional filled matches in PCW history. Both men fought with all of their hearts and then some. The match came to a end when Brock reversed a Steele powerbomb into a X-Factor and freed Jacobs. As Brock embraced his girlfriend, a most drastic change happened. As Brock urged Tiffany on to kick the downed Steele, Tiffany turned and kicked Brock in the junk, to the shock of fans and everybody else watching. Steele, Jacobs and Bruno preceded to beatdown the exhausted Newbludd as the fans threw garbage in the ring.

The turn on Jacobs brought a new twist to the heated rivalry, no longer did Brock have to fight for someone else, he fought for revenge. Judas and his new partner Cain Manson Crow won the tag straps soon after, but the reign did not last long. Soon thereafter, to the shock of the wrestling world, Judas Steele died of a drug overdose in a unknown location. Brock was put into a deep depression by the loss of his arch-rival. But, the loss of Judas would bring about the rejuvenation of Newbludd’s career. For, the Tag Team titles were vacated and at the funeral of Steele, the tag titles were up for grabs. Somewhere in the graveyard, the two tag belts were waiting for their new owners. As Brock opened up Judas’s casket to place a beer in his casket, he did not find a dead corpse, but a PCW tag team belt. The other winner of the belt, was Brock’s best friend in PCW, newcomer Stephen Blood.

So, on a day of mourning and sadness the Blood Brothers were born and the PCW tag scene has never been the same. Brock and Stephen managed to score the tag belts, a unprecedented four times. Beating such teams as Sex and Violence, Da Wiseguys and the Media Assassins. The Blood Brothers will go down into the annuls of PCW history as probably the greatest tag team to grace a PCW ring. 

“The Innovators” future on PCW looks very bright. He recently scored his first PCW singles gold by beating “The Mack” Eddie for the PCW Extreme title. But, then lost it to his  best friend and tag team partner, “The New Legend” Stephen Blood.

Brock then shortly thereafter retired and has comeback a couple of times, once with a stint in “Old School” to battle Ivan Stanislavs Red Army. But, he was quickly cut short by a kidney injury.

Now, Brock is in a new federation, with a new attitude and is ready to do what he does best, humiliate people.

Now, with the World Title around his waist, he's on top of the world.

tenures.bio:
The story of Marvin Harris is a long and complicated one beginning on the hot evening of February 6th, 1972 in a lower-middle class suburb of Panama City, Florida. Born the middle of three children to Lara and Jacob Harris, a dockworker and housewife, he had a fairly average childhood. He never managed to make an impact scholastically, unlike his older brother Monty, or become a sports hero like his younger brother Mike. Marvin always kind of shied away from social situations and remained perpetually average as far as talent goes. That all changed when he discovered pro-wrestling.

What started out as primitive backyard antics between brothers soon blossomed into a part-time hobby in college and later finally became Marvin's career ambition. He had a rough time selling his family on the idea, but after constant pressure they caved to his wishes and sent him off to a local wrestler's school. It was in this environment he flourished, Marvin's natural ability and skill was evident to his teachers. Finally, after a three-month stint of training he was released to go and make himself in the business.

He started out wrestling under the un-inspiring moniker “Marvelous” Marvin Harris, a man who asked for nothing more than fair matches and his shot at success. But, the cutthroat nature of the wrestling profession soon became apparent to Marvin as loss after loss were delivered to him due to dirty tricks by his opponents. As his frustration grew, he was advised by his comrades to seek the help of one of the world's leading pro-wrestling psychiatrists, Professor Sickman B. Fraud.

Unfortunately, the infamous Professor Fraud, a cruel and twisted man himself, had no intention of curing Marvin of his losing streak. Instead, he began a long process that corrupted Marvin's mind with bizarre untested psychoactive drugs and grueling hours of intense subconscious suggestion. What finally emerged was no longer the timid and fair 'Marvelous' Marvin Harris, but a depraved and reckless individual that wouldn't rule out any underhanded deed in order to secure the easy win.

It was at this point that Marvin began adorning his trademark gasmask, a delusional by-product of Professor Fraud's demented brainwashing. He wrestled for years under the watchful eye of Fraud, who'd reward a victory with further treatment and failure with vicious mental and physical torture. However, Fraud finally pushed Marvin too far one night and in retaliation Marvin unflinchingly broke the professor's fragile neck.

Marvin had little time to enjoy his freedom though, as soon after the incident he was beaten into a coma by Fraud's personal henchmen, two former assault convicts that Fraud had made into asylum orderlies. He spent the next six months completely out of action. When he finally awoke, he jumped right back into the fray. He competed at a new level of intensity and skill, but without Fraud's discipline, however brutal, he was also out of control. He rampaged through numerous underground federations (most of them Justin Lollie promotions) and became relatively infamous for occasionally breaking an opponent's arms or legs. He continued along this downward spiral until learning of Fraud's return. He tried fleeing his former torturer by enrolling himself into the Primetime Wrestling Academy; the last place he figured the mentally unbalanced shrink would look for him.

Unfortunately, Marvin had underestimated the PTC's renown and after only his second television promo for the academy Professor Fraud found him. Fraud, who had used his legal authority as Marvin's psychiatrist, had him once more committed into an asylum. Once more under Fraud's supervision, Marvin was tortured and prodded into becoming a monster. Throughout his time in the PWA he continually escaped the asylum and wreaked havoc before being caught, often because people who he'd believed were friends and family had sold him out.

When he was finally promoted into the XWA he was astonished that Professor Fraud had inexplicably decided to release him from custody. Despite the fact he believed a trick was played on him by his old nemesis, he reveled in his newfound freedom and had numerous strange adventures in trying to secure employment, friends, and most importantly a love life. Marvin then found himself once more promoted, this time into RUSH wrestling, but the freedom he once cherished so much began to turn on him. He became increasingly reckless and lackluster in performance, until an odd meeting with his brother led to his reuniting with both of his siblings along with another psychiatrist, one who seemed the exact opposite of Fraud. Marvin felt like, in this new atmosphere, he could really begin to heal from the deep psychological wounds imposed on him by Professor Fraud, but then Scott Cage came along.

It started as a simple spat over damaging Cage's truck in an accident and soon led to an extremely dangerous game of one-upmanship involving fast moving vehicles and the lives of innocent people, gaining drastic momentum with Marvin winning the RUSH Network Title. It finally ended in a bloody, career-threatening 'Hell on Wheels' match at the first Ignition PPV. It was there that Marvin Harris went through a windshield and head (or rather mask) first into a tree trunk, causing a severe concussion that turned into a coma. There, for five months, he remained motionless, no signs of brain activity. Until on the evening of October 13th, 2002 when he miraculously awoke with only one thing on his mind; revenge.

tenures.bio:
Mr.Uk. was born to a wealthy Crumpet making company boss. His mother and father lived great lives, in the lap of luxury. Mr.Uk. spent pointless hours reading through books at his boarding school, as his fathers business looked to be getting stronger and stronger.

One day, after meeting someone he enjoyed being with, a girl named Melissa, he took a trip into the poor school in the middle of a very run down estate. There people brawled, scrapped and generally fought over nothing.

Someone teased him about his posh tank tops and posh accent. Wasting no time, he unleashed a clenched fist and took the 'kid' down.

Generally he hated people being hurt, but the rush he had and the adrenaline pumped through hard.

Thoroughly enjoying hitting people though was a trouble, and so he looked for other ways of forcing himself to attain the same adrenaline rush as hitting someone.

He saw wrestling on, where such greats as Bret Hart and Shawn Michaels fought for the supremacy of the mat, and to win a victory.

Mr.Uk. became instantly hooked. He immediately began training with a top wrestling, who taught him the technical side of wrestling, and said weapons should never be relied on for the win. Releasing competition was only hot in America, he headed on over to the other side of the Atlantic.

He joined some 'bush league' federations and swept the board aside with his amazing technical wrestling skills. Dominating the fed, he only lost once, before being spotted by the PCW.

PCW was on the rise and he joined up straight away.

Forming the European Union with three other European based stars he generally enjoyed himself, until injuries and lack of time with wife Nikki, led him to quit.

He spent some 18 months in the wilderness, before heading back to WT to sign with RUSH.

Mr.Uk. is an arrogant asshole, prepared to do anything for his country or for himself.

Good looking, great with the mic and an awesome wrestling, what more could you want?

name: Ukyo Matsuura

tenures.style: Ukyo works strictly off using speed to his advantage, using evasion and escapes as his defensive tactics. His offense is based on using the opponent’s slowness to his advantage, and as he evades and escapes the opponent’s offense he strikes with his own. He works a lucha-libre-like style offense / defense system, where it’s very hard to get a hand on him. He calls his style the Hyper-MAX style, as his swift reaction makes everyone else look like they’re in slow motion.

caption: Heir to the puroresu legend Naizen Matsuura, Ukyo Matsuura teamed with Basho Amuro as the Mega Soaring Arrows through the winter of 2003 into 2004.

name: Basho Amuro

tenures.style: Basho is opposite to Ukyo, a shoot-fighter based tactician. He revolves his offense around a Ground and Pound technique, take the opponent down with technical maneuvers and beat him into submission with stiff strikes. He uses his share of power moves, not to mention a few hard kicks to the chin and face to knock the opponent down. His defense involves reversing grapples, and countering strikes with harder strikes of his own. In Japan he used to be known as “Three Strikes” because no one could stand against his three-strike combo; no one has been left standing.

caption: The Violence Poet out of Osaka held the Tag Team Championship with Ukyo Matsuura as the Mega Soaring Arrows.

tenures.bio:
Born in Newark, New Jersey, Chris Bagwell grew up as would any other child with a dream.  However, Chris' dream was separate from others whom later became wrestler superstars.

All through childhood, Chris struggled to achieve a dream of becoming a famous football player for the New York Giants.  Up until college, Chris lived out his dream by participating in recreational leagues and on his high school team.

Bagwell eventually got a football scholarship to Rutgers University in his Senior year in high school.  To celebrate, his friends took him out to a bar and they went non a drinking brigade.  Little did he realize, his life was about to take a major turn.

The bar Bagwell and his friends had went to that night was home to a gang.  It was the gang's 'pool meeting' night.  Where they basically took over the bar, shot pool, drank, and discussed whatever gangs like to discuss.  The average drinker avoided the local bar on those Thursday nights because of the fear they contained for the gang.  But Bagwell and his football buddies didn't give a crap.  They were out to have a good time and they did just so.

At first, all was well and the gang didn't mind too much.  It wasn't until one of the members approached a friend of Bagwell in jealousy and started a fight.  The gang began to assault the friend of Bagwell in an all out brawl.  Each of Bagwell's buddies were hesitant to jump in at first.  Their thoughts didn't change much when 3 of the gang members pulled out blades to hold the football guys off.

Bagwell held off at first...until he saw the face of his close friend, Yoko Shorskiny, covered in blood and looking in fear.  Bagwell tightly grasped his shot glass and pitched it at the back of the head of one of the gang members.  Bagwell then got off his stool, raised it above his head, and whacked it across the faces of the three men with the blades.  Bagwell ran right to the middle of the fight, where it was a 5 on 1 assault on Yoko.  He tackled one of the guys to the ground, hitting another on the way down.  Bagwell started throwing his fists until recieving a devistating kick to the gut from the gang member he knocked off balance.

Bagwell was knocked to the ground and rolled over.  Two of the gang members started kicking him in the face as he tried shielding himself.  He then caught a glimpse of one of the knives and quickly reached for it.  He immediately threw his arm up and gashed both of the attackers across the chest and arm.  All he saw was blood spill.  He kicked his legs at the attackers, pushing them away.  At this time, his 2 other friends who weren't involved already fled.  Bagwell got to his feet and delivered a gash across the face of one of the 3 attacking Yoko.  He then stabbed another in the lower ab.  And for the third, he delivered a solid punch across the face.

Bagwell lifted Shorskiny to his feet and the two made a run for it.  Sirens could be heard blocks away.  However, Bagwell and Shorskiny made a successfull escape.  Shorskiny was losing blood and fast.  They escaped into an alley and Bagwell tore off his shirt to held clog the blood so Shorskiny didn't lose anymore.  A black Dodge Viper then pulled up.  A man stepped out with first aid equiptment and nursed Shorskiny as best he could.  He gave Bagwell a few sprays and faceclothes to clean himself off.

The man explained that he was Ricky Michaels, a local promoter.  He went on to say that he was witness to the whole fight and saw the retaliation of Bagwell.  He then made Bagwell and Shorskiny an unrefusable offer.  He demanded that they sign a 1 year contract with his promotion as professional wrestlers.  At first, Bagwell declined immediately.  That was, until Michaels threatened to turn the two in.

Michaels was clearly the only man who could help the two.  They had no choice but to accept the offer.  Accepting the offer rid Bagwell of his scholarship to Rutgers University.  The year had passed and Bagwell left the company.  Seeing as there being no alternative lifestyle for him, Shorskiny signed a contract extention which later separated the two friends.

Bagwell was in a dilemma, no longer having a full scholarship and not having the money to pay for a full college education.  He began playing football for minor leagues and working a wide variety of jobs to build his savings account.  Another year passed and the minor league team he played for was falling apart.  Bagwell was left with nothing to do on a canceled game day and wondered around town.  He found a flier for a wrestling event that afternoon.  For old time's sake, he called and was luckily enough to purchase one of the remaining 10 tickets.

The event went well and Bagwell actually enjoyed the relaxation.  The main event rolled around and he saw a man he hadn't talked to in a year.  Yoko Shorskiny entered the ring and gave Bagwell a brief, glassy stare.  Neither man spoke words to each other.  Shorskiny's opponent entered the ring.  The current Champion, DJ.  Moments into the match and foru large men raced to the ring.  They began to assault Shorskiny in the ring.

Bagwell's history flashed before his eyes.  He remembered the bar fight.  He rose from his chair and folded it up.  He hopped the guardrail and dove into the ring.  Bagwell planted the chair over each of the 4 fat men's heads until it was kicked out of his hands by DJ.  The two began to exchange hits.  Bagwell eventually flattened out DJ in the end, causing the five men to flee.  It was thast night when Bagwell and Yoko's friendship was restored.

Seeing no other alternative, Bagwell signed a contract to the promotion until it went extinct.  Bagwell never decided to leave the wrestling business again.  He stuck with it with his good friend, Yoko Shorskiny until the two eventually recieved separate deals and parted ways once more.

To this day, Bagwell doesn't know what compelled him to enter wrestling. A hobby he hated so dearly...now he lived his life for.  How odd things turn out.

PCW's own air says where this broadcaster came from and then keeps saying it. Its Sabotage of 29 April 2001 has two colleagues work it out aloud — “where did Steven come from originally?”, answered “UFW, I think” — and conclude that he “is the only ex UFW'er booked to appear in any capacity tonight”. Its Fusion of 13 October 2000 has an Ultra Fantasy Wrestling arrival call him “the gold-hungry bastard that we all knew and loved at UFW”, and Smith answer that a running gag about him “was an angle played up in UFW”. Its Turmoil of 24 October 2000 has a colleague ask whether his verdict covers “the matches with Xtreme you called back in the days of the UFW”, and its Turmoil of 23 January 2001 has him recall calling Lightning Kid's matches there. Ultra Fantasy Wrestling's own staff page names Steven Smith among its commentators and its interviewers. Four shows naming the federation, an on-air angle carried across, and the first federation's own crew list: one man, one record.

The fed's biography card (accession 0159), bio 12486, is this record: The AWC card's text: 'No relation of his namesake The British Bomber, Smith is the weakest third of the old PCW team and was replaced by Duke Williams in the latter portion of the great promotion's existence'. This man's own PCW farewell traces the road himself. On its Sabotage of 22 July 2001 he says: “To UFW, where one of the illustrious members of the Von Smackdown family, Groan, took me under his wing and allowed me to blossom before him. Where I battled such giants as Nemesis... UFW, where I met Professor Herbert Dorkiman, who I later followed to wrestling utopia. From UFW to MWF... From MWF to PCW”. The same show runs his entrance video through three federations in order and shows him “standing at the top of the UFW ramp alongside Groan, Lightning Kid, X-Con, and Genocide” — four names on Ultra Fantasy Wrestling's own final member list and title ledgers — and a send-off that remembers him in “the hearts of AWS, UFW and PCW fans alike”. Ultra Fantasy Wrestling's own Titleholder History records his Rising Star reign from 19 June 2000 and his Hardcore reign from 13 July. A career narrated leg by leg from the second federation's own air, naming four verifiable stablemates and opponents: one man, one record.

Appearance:Once noted for his sqeaky clean 'pretty boy' apperance,the Wes of today is almost a totally different figure.His blonde hair has been replaced with short black messy hair.Wes has a trim black 

goatee which connects to a thin black mustach overhis top lip,Wes also wears a small pointed patch of hair under his bottom lip.He has rings in his left eyebrow as well as both ears.He he uses rather sublte expressions when engaged in conversation making it very hard to read his disposition,with a small 

nose,high cheekbones, and  brilliant green eyes.He has slinder but rather toned build.A tatoo of a red star is on the back of his neck,and he has the words 'Enter Omega' tatooed on his left shoulder.Wes also rejects the 'superficial and shallow' practice of most wrestler and does not wax his chest hair,so he has a small amount of hair down his chest and stomach.Outside of the ring Wes normally wears slightly baggy and well worn jeans with black boots that are always polished to a mirror shine,he normally wears T-shirt's that are cheaply made and support one of his various political causes.In the ring he wears much the same minus the T-shirts,as he feels that money could be put to better use than to buy wrestling tights.

tenures.bio: Ming was born into a rich family in Beijing, China. His father was a high ranking official in the Communist Administration, his mother was a dutiful society wife. Ming had everything: cars, land, women. Whatever he wanted was his at the expense of the proletariat his father professed to serve. Ming soon grew bored of his pampered lifestyle and delved into more and more dangerous activities in a futile attempt to stave off the amazing boredom that he felt the world presented him. In the process Ming was gravely injured in a freak Boa Constrictor accident. Ming soon realized that true danger was not for him, and so he enrolled in a pro wrestling school in a misguided attempt to find a 'safe' environment in which to get his thrills. Of course, all did not pan out as he might have hoped. Ming was not offered a huge contract, he was not put over by his various promotors (who were offended by Ming's constant use of the terms 'peon' and references to what he did to their respective mothers the night previous) and he did not make a name for himself. That is, until he joined the UFW where he defeated 'The Scholar' Howard Porter for the Rising Star Title. However, perhaps because of the 'Ming Curse' that he constantly blames for his various bunglings and failures, UFW shut down a week later. Ming moved on to the MWF in a UFW Invasion angle, but soon grew bored. Ming left the world of wrestling to pursue other activities. After his attempt at writing the great Chinese novel failed misreably, Ming decided to make his triumphant return. He joined PCW, tricked the now (in)famous Red Army into accepting him into their ranks, then turned on them and joined the newly formed Elements with stablemates Inphino Blitz, Miyagawa, and Kensuke Suzahara. Ming became a face, but never felt comfortable in that role, constantly being tempted by his inner heel to commit evil deeds. Ming managed to stave off his anti-social tendencies long enough to win the PCW Tag Team Titles with his sometimes friend Inphino Blitz, but soon grew burnt out after being booked on five cards in a row. Ming quit wrestling again, and was not to be seen for 9 months, when he made his triumphant return to wrestling in the fledgling fed known as FSW where he returned to his heelish roots.
